newsitem.title: USA: Dunavant sees more imports if U.S. cotton stays up.
newsitem.headline: Dunavant sees more imports if U.S. cotton stays up.

text.p: Cotton imports will continue to flood the U.S. marketplace as long as domestic prices remain high and world prices comparatively low, said leading cotton merchant William B. Dunavant.

Speaking to a committee of National Cotton Council (NCC) Wednesday in a session closed to reporters, Dunavant said, "The American textile industry needs imports to be competitive," according to an NCC release issued Thursday.
Problems with last season's domestic supply put an added burden on merchants to import raw cotton. "We had to go out and get cotton to supply our customes," Dunavant said.
Also, Dunavant said USDA's estimate of a crop of 17.9 million bales was unexpected, especially after hearing state-by-state reports indicating a stronger crop.

China, in the meantime, is not likely to buy substantial amounts of U.S. cotton in the near term. "The U.S. has been China's favorite supplier for years, but it (China) is now looking at other growths because they are cheaper," Dunavant said.
